phases.name: Phase 1 — Establish the exposure (blocks the ruling)

tasks.title: MEASURE it retroactively before designing anything, the repo's refute-before-building discipline. Replay every initiative's log and find every plan_updated that took a phase or task from a resolved status (done/dropped/blocked) back to pending or omitted. Publish the count, name the records and the events. If it is ZERO across 37 records, the hazard is theoretical and the ruling changes shape — say so rather than building for it.

Establish whether the hole is MCP-only or dialect-wide. `sofar event append --type plan_updated` bypasses any tool-layer merge entirely, and the MCP-less convention dialect uses exactly that path (phase-lifecycle D1). Read cli/event.ts's append against mcp/update-plan.ts and state which callers a tool-boundary fix would and would not cover.

Separate the two candidate defects. Does SPEC promise full-replace to CALLERS, and do the tool description and docs tell an agent it must restate statuses? A contract nobody is told about is a documentation defect, not a missing merge, and it has a much cheaper fix. Answer this before 2.1 picks a mechanism.

DECIDE the mechanism. (a) Merge at the TOOL boundary: update_plan folds current state and carries status forward for matching phase names and task ids unless the caller supplies one — the appended payload stays a COMPLETE plan, so plan_updated's on-disk full-replace contract and replay determinism are both untouched. (b) Merge in the FOLD: preserve status when the payload omits it — the one option that changes how every historical log folds, and therefore the one that can break replay determinism. (c) Detect only: a doctor axis and a warning when a plan_updated drops a resolved status, contract unchanged, loss made visible. (d) Nothing: document the convention. Log the decision citing task-drop-state D2 and phase-lifecycle M2.

DECIDE what protects the closes already written, if 2.1 leaves any window open. 34 phase closes across 16 STILL-ACTIVE records are the concrete thing this initiative exists to stop losing, and they are erasable by the next ordinary replan in any of those records. This is a separate question from the mechanism and must not be assumed answered by it.
Implement whatever 2.1 chose. Schema lives ONLY in packages/schema/src if the ruling needs schema at all — the guard-rail holds.

Tests: a replan omitting statuses preserves them; an explicit status in the payload still wins over the carried one; replay stays deterministic over every existing log; and the MCP-less dialect behaves as the ruling says it should, rather than as an untested afterthought.
docs/SPEC.md is authoritative: the full-replace wording either changes or gains its carve-out, plus §Acceptance criteria. No task is done until its criteria pass.

payload.text:
ORIGIN — the evidence this initiative was opened on, carried over from phase-lifecycle's final review (event 01KZXTVFE6D48GZAEBZGH36X78, commit 3353f3d) so it does not have to be rediscovered.

THE MECHANISM, verified in code 2026-08-13 on engine 0.27.0:
- mcp/update-plan.ts is four lines of body: resolveWriteInitiative, then appendAndProject('plan_updated', {plan: args.plan}). It appends the caller's payload verbatim. There is no read of current state and no merge.
- core/fold.ts:1085-1091 rebuilds state.phases from that payload: `status: phase.status ?? 'pending'` for phases and `status: task.status ?? 'pending'` for tasks.
- The tool's own description says it plainly: "Replace the entire plan (goal + phases with tasks) — a full replace, not a merge."

So a plan_updated that omits statuses resets every phase to pending and every task to pending. Nothing warns, because nothing is wrong: the fold is doing exactly what it was told. The loss is only visible to someone who remembers what the record used to say.

WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING NOW rather than a curiosity: this is the documented contract for TASKS and has been survivable because agents restate task statuses as a matter of course (every real plan_updated payload in this repo's 37 records carries them). Phases were different — phase status was barely written before sofar_update_phase shipped in 0.27.0, so there was little to lose. That changed on 2026-08-13: phase-lifecycle 4.3 wrote 34 retroactive phase closes into 16 records that are all still ACTIVE. One ordinary replan in any of them, by an agent that hand-builds a plan from prose rather than from the folded state, silently re-inflates the repo-wide stale-phase count from 1 back toward 35 with no signal that anything was lost.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN, and is why Phase 1 exists before the ruling: whether this has EVER actually happened. The retroactive scan in 1.1 is the honest first move — if no plan_updated in 37 records has ever dropped a resolved status, the defect is a latent one and the right answer may be documentation (1.3) or detection (2.1c) rather than a merge.

THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS FIX: merging in the FOLD (2.1b) looks like the natural home and is the one option that changes how every historical log folds, which is exactly what SPEC's replay-determinism and forward-compatibility guarantees forbid. Merging at the TOOL boundary (2.1a) leaves the appended event a complete plan, so the on-disk contract never moves — but it does not cover `sofar event append --type plan_updated`, which is the MCP-less dialect's only path (phase-lifecycle D1). That asymmetry is 1.2.

NOT bound to a branch: created with --no-bind, because main is bound to drift-certification and three peer sessions were live on it. Pin this record explicitly with sofar_start_session; do not rebind main out from under them.

payload.text:
INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION from the stale-session-signals session, 2026-08-13, verified against the tree at 0.28.0 rather than taken from the message that reported it. Both cited sites read exactly as described: mcp/update-plan.ts appends `{plan: args.plan}` verbatim with no carry-forward, and the fold's plan_updated case does `state.phases = p.plan.phases.map(...)` with `status: phase.status ?? 'pending'` for phases AND for tasks — a full replace, so every status set BEFORE a replan and not restated in it is silently reset. Later task_status_changed events replay on top, which is why the loss is invisible in a record that keeps working: only the un-restated history goes.

MEASURED EXPOSURE, by scanning all 37 records rather than the repair alone: 19 records carry phase closes from this window (47 closes). 13 of those are STILL ACTIVE — 29 closes that an ordinary replan would erase with no signal. Exactly one record has already had a plan_updated land after a phase close: phase-lifecycle itself, 5 phases closed then replanned, and NOTHING was dropped — that replan carried every status forward. So the hazard is real and armed, and has not yet fired. Worth knowing for Phase 1's measurement: the honest answer so far is zero occurrences, which makes this a prevention rather than a repair, and makes the carry-forward design the whole deliverable.
